pack_name: KYE Chain of Authority for Iron Mountain InSight DXP

claim_set.claim_text: Every consequential AI action on a record custodied or classified in Iron Mountain InSight DXP MUST map to a recorded named-authority decision — the agent, the record, the intended consequential action, and the named human under whose authority it proceeds. Actions lacking a recorded authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate. Iron Mountain proves where information travelled; KYE proves who was authorised to act on it.

Before a consequential action proceeds, the record's InSight custody and classification context (record identity, chain-of-custody event history, InSight classification, mapped from ISO 23081 via the connector) MUST be bound into the named-authority decision and its evidence pin — the custody->authority binding (Chain of Custody -> Chain of Authority).

Before a consequential action proceeds it MUST carry a recorded due-diligence result — a competence / authority-scope determination, a permitted-use check, and the classification-driven authority bar (a higher InSight sensitivity classification raises the authority threshold). An unscreened, low-confidence, or classification-bar-failing action is refused.

An AI-driven irreversible or high-impact action on an InSight-custodied record MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT commit until a named human records sign-off (§36 GovernedUI); a regulated/restricted InSight classification additionally requires §36 two-person sign-off. The accountable human remains personally accountable; accountability does not transfer to the AI.

KYE governs WHETHER an InSight-custodied record may drive a consequential action and under whose authority, and PROVES the basis. KYE does NOT do IDP, store records, classify records, or run records-retention. KYE retains PROOF-OF-GOVERNANCE (its own evidence chain), NOT Iron Mountain's records. AI-ready data is not enough — you need authority-ready AI.
